### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dabf8d795ee9279c18b4b00bfabb322544106b2f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1259b0454b4d735940d3fa7d3e4afadf36dcaa8f` — the merge of head `fd206c3164f033f08ba9b06caa7afc6864b5b3f7` into base `dabf8d795ee9279c18b4b00bfabb322544106b2f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1259b0454b4d735940d3fa7d3e4afadf36dcaa8f && git checkout 1259b0454b4d735940d3fa7d3e4afadf36dcaa8f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dabf8d795ee9279c18b4b00bfabb322544106b2f fd206c3164f033f08ba9b06caa7afc6864b5b3f7 && git checkout -B drift-repro dabf8d795ee9279c18b4b00bfabb322544106b2f && git merge --no-ff fd206c3164f033f08ba9b06caa7afc6864b5b3f7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dabf8d795ee9279c18b4b00bfabb322544106b2f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dabf8d795ee9279c18b4b00bfabb322544106b2f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Isolated at-tier reviewer subagent, run by the `domain:spec` seat-4 session on the maintainer's instruction in that session (「帮我处理」, with the landing route chosen there); every one of its 54 transcript turns served at the tier the constant names. Adopted by the seat 2026-09-24T05:35Z. The record below is the reviewer's, unedited except the two header lines.


Refs read: `refs/review/pr-19898` = `fd206c3164f033f08ba9b06caa7afc6864b5b3f7` (2 commits over merge-base `1f89ba0d704a797225ab8cf306e4cdec89edae8e`; PR base `dabf8d795ee9279c18b4b00bfabb322544106b2f` is an ancestor of `origin/main` = `c1641868a3da71537c9c6c572d2bd2044103236b`). Ruling B is card comment `5791822697` on #19527 (items 1–3). `pulls/19898/files`: 6 files, all under `packages/lint/src/` plus one `.changeset/` entry; no review threads; `commits/fd206c3164…/check-runs`: 34 runs, 31 success, 3 skipped (Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in), 0 failures — Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1–6, Governed Surface Queue Guard, single-writer-path and same-issue guards all green.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set / behaviour: none moves — verified, not trusted.** For each of the three source files the non-comment changed-line filter is empty: `git diff origin/main refs/review/pr-19898 -- packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -vE '^(\+\+\+|---)' | grep -vE '^[+-]\s*(//|\*|/\*)'` → (empty); same for `reference-integrity-suite.ts` and `runtime-gate.ts`. `validate-ai-tool-references.ts` (the emitter, `AI_SKILL_TOOL_UNRESOLVED` at `:39`, `severity: 'warning'` at `:226`, three-limb `collectToolUniverse` at `:144-165`) is not in the PR file list. `AUTHORING_COMMANDS = ['validate', 'build', 'lint']` at `refs/review/pr-19898:packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts:153` is unchanged; the `validateReferenceIntegrity` entry keeps `commands: ALL` (`:813`) and `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'view', 'object', 'dataset', 'report']` (`:939`). Correct against ruling B: the whole-stack verdict is exactly where it was.

**Regression in loudness: none, because no door judged `skill` before.** At `origin/main`: `git grep -nE "runtimeTypes.*skill" origin/main -- 'packages/lint/src/*.ts' ':!packages/lint/src/*.test.ts'` returns only a comment line (`reference-integrity-suite.ts:463`), and `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY` (`origin/main:packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts:75-175`) has no `skill:` row. Mechanically the door returns before any judgement: `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor` filters `AUTHORING_RULES` by `runtimeTypes` (`refs/review/pr-19898:packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts:549-554`); `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` has `if (rules.length === 0) return empty;` at `:891`, ahead of the snapshot builder, which itself returns `null` for an unmapped type at `:622-623`. So a genuinely unresolved tool on a `skill` write was silent at the door on `main` and is silent at head; `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` warned before and warn after. The ruling asked for exactly this (item 1: NEVER emitted by the door).

**Ruling item 1 (restate the hold-out and its two pins as by-design, citing the ruling; LIT stays): done, right.** `authoring-rules.ts:907-931` (the `skill` block on the `validateReferenceIntegrity` entry), `runtime-gate.ts:161-166`, `reference-integrity-suite.ts:463-506` (the member's docblock, which on the base still prescribed route A: "Crossing it needs `actions` / `tools` carried in `RuntimeStackContext` + `CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS`…") now all cite `5791822697` and drop the route-A direction. The two DARK pins keep their assertions (`runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('skill')` → `[]`, `stackKeyForType('skill')` → null, `runtimeGatedTypes()` not containing `skill`; member `runtimeTypes` not containing `skill`) with reason strings restated (`runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts:513-534`); the LIT case 「one skill, one rule, two universes」 is kept at `:610-680` and its snapshot-bound message now reads a red as a widening of `RuntimeStackContext` against item 3 rather than as "cross `skill` now" — the right reading.

**Ruling item 2 (report which shape the guard allows, land that one): reported OUTSIDE, and the reasoning holds.** The guard is over `runtimeGatedTypes()` (`refs/review/pr-19898:packages/lint/src/authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts:383-393`), which is DERIVED from rule declarations (`runtime-gate.ts:556-563`); with no rule declaring `skill`, the invariant asks nothing of it. The two alternatives are both refused by the ruling or by the table's own note (`runtime-gate.ts:93-99`, the `seed: 'data'` inert-mapping shape). No rule was invented.

**Ruling item 3 (no snapshot widening): honoured.** `CONTEXT_STACK_KEY_ORDER` at `runtime-gate.ts:510-515` is `objects, permissions, books, datasets`, unchanged; `RuntimeStackContext` (`:281`) is untouched (comment-only diff); `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is not in the file list and its door still hands exactly those four collections (`refs/review/pr-19898:packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts:675-680`, `CLOSURE_CONTEXT_KEY_BY_TYPE` at `:397-402`).

**New pins: weight-bearing on the ruling's two halves.** (a) `it.each` over three tool names through the real door asserts `errors []`, `advisories []`, `rulesRun []` and, in the same process, that the undispatched member DOES fire on the builder-derived door snapshot (`inert-type-writes.test.ts:571-596`) — crossing `skill` on the entry turns `rulesRun` non-empty and red. (a') no gated type maps to `skills` and `skills` is not a context key (`:598-609`). (b) `runAuthoringRules` over every `AUTHORING_COMMANDS` value on a stack carrying `actions` reports exactly `[{ path: 'skills[1].tools[0]', severity: 'warning' }]` (`:611-631`) — deleting the member or the `stack.actions` limb reds it; the runner reads `run.parsed ?? run.normalized` (`authoring-rules.ts` `runAuthoringRules` body), so the `{ normalized }` call reaches the `parsed`-input entry. (c) the guard invariant over the real tables plus a `skill` write's `rulesRun` → `[]` (`:529-545`).

**Governing text truthfully restated.** ADR-0109 Decision §3 at `origin/main:docs/adr/0109-ai-tool-authoring-model.md:69-77` names `validate-ai-tool-references` in `@objectstack/lint`, the universe `stack.tools` ∪ platform registry ∪ the materialised `action_` family from `stack.actions` and objects' actions, severity warning, and "a runtime plugin outside the registry remains statically invisible, and the runtime deliberately tolerates unresolved names" — matching the new comments and the changeset body.

**Left advising falsely: nothing found.** Every downstream reader of the rule id describes an `os validate` / whole-stack verdict, which is the ruled state: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx:165-166`, `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx:91-93`, `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts:393-395`, `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts:372-373`, `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:85`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts:17` (all at `refs/review/pr-19898`). The docs-drift-flagged page `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` mentions `skill` only at `:717` (a formula-skill link); its runtime-publish column never listed `skill`, so it needs no edit. `git grep -n "on a measurement" refs/review/pr-19898 -- packages/lint` → only the history paragraph in the test file (`:485`), which is deliberate.

**Required and missing: nothing.** **Beyond the ruling: nothing functional** (see ③ for the file-surface note).

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/lint` (`.changeset/19527-skill-tool-verdict-whole-stack.md`, package at `17.4.0`, all packages in one `fixed` group per `.changeset/config.json`). Correct ceiling and floor: no export, type, authorable key, accept set or runtime string moves (comment-only source diff, verified above), so `minor` is unavailable; `skip-changeset` is reserved by `origin/main:AGENTS.md:1081-1085` for a diff that publishes nothing from a released package, and this package publishes `dist` built by tsup (`packages/lint/package.json:32`, `packages/lint/tsup.config.ts`), where the repo's own recorded measurements say source comments ride into `dist/*.js` (`.changeset/17676-package-registry-docblock-capability-name.md:15`, `.changeset/18614-conversion-registry-retryconfig-liveness-claim.md:9` — the latter a registry-array entry comment in a tsup-built package, the same position as the three blocks here; `.changeset/16270-org-record-tab-strip-provenance.md:42-44`). `Clause-②: no` in the PR body is right (nothing widens or narrows); AGENTS.md `:1095-1096` requires the line inside the changeset body only for a breaking changeset. `Check Changeset` is green at head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **non-blocking — file surface wider than the claim's literal list.** Claim comment `5796885591` named `authoring-rules.ts`, "its two pins", `runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts`, the wiring file and `.changeset/`; the PR also edits `packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts` (the member docblock that still prescribed route A) and `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.datasource-writes.test.ts` (a third pin restating "held out on the measurement"). Both are comment-only restatements of the same hold-out, inside the claimed package; the claim's census declared only `authoring-rules.ts` and `runtime-gate*` CLEAR and did not census `reference-integrity-suite.ts`, but the `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` check-run is success at head.
- **non-blocking — one stale wording left.** `refs/review/pr-19898:packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts:161` still reads "`skill` is held out — asserted absent in its own block, not here." Test-file comment, not shipped; the ruling's restatement asked for "by design" wording.
- **non-blocking — the pending #19474 changeset still publishes the rejected route.** `origin/main:.changeset/19474-six-inert-runtime-create-doors.md:25` ends "Crossing it needs `actions` / `tools` carried in `RuntimeStackContext` … and its own card." It is another card's unconsumed input and out of this claim; when both compile into the same CHANGELOG the later entry supersedes it, but a reader grepping the rule id will meet the route-A prescription first.
- **non-blocking — whole-stack judgement is not reached on runtime-mint paths, by ruling.** `skill` is `allowRuntimeCreate: true` (`origin/main:packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:1199`); a skill written through Studio / REST `/meta` / MCP passes the metadata-protocol door with no tool-reference verdict (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts:667-680` → `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` → early return), and only the CLI callers (`packages/cli/src/commands/{validate,compile,lint}.ts`, `utils/artifact-packages.ts`, `utils/scaffold-validate.ts`) reach `validateAiToolReferences`. This is the state on `origin/main` and the outcome ruling B chose over route A; recorded so the maintainer sees the accepted gap named, not because the PR changed it.
- **non-blocking — the "plugin-registered tool" leg is mechanically the "exists nowhere" leg.** `acme_plugin_lookup` is registered by nothing in the test, so the member treats it exactly as `no_such_tool_anywhere`; the pin still holds (door silent, member fires), the label is narrative.
- **non-blocking — dist comment survival not re-measured here.** The changeset's rationale rests on the dev's stated rebuild measurement (3 hits per dist file) and on the three repo precedents cited under ②; per the review contract no build was run locally.
- No deviation from ruling items 1–3; no pin found that fails to bear weight; no governed surface touched (`GOVERNED_SURFACES` at `origin/main:scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs:1055-1061` lists `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` — none in the file list).
